stem: Which action is appropriate for a client with a chest tube connected to a drainage system?

options.A: Place the drainage system on the bed at approximately chest level during routine care.
options.B: Keep the drainage system upright and below the level of the client's chest or insertion site.
options.C: Raise the drainage system above chest level during repositioning to reduce tubing length.
options.D: Clamp the chest tube routinely during transport even when no specific indication exists.

rationale: Current NCBI/StatPearls chest-tube guidance states that the drainage system should be positioned below chest level to prevent fluid or air backflow. Nursing guidance in NCBI Bookshelf also specifies keeping the drainage unit upright and below the client's chest or insertion site and advises against routine clamping because of the risk of tension pneumothorax. Therefore B is correct. A and C place the system too high and can promote backflow, while D uses clamping without an appropriate indication.
educational_objective: Maintain chest-tube drainage equipment upright and below chest/insertion-site level and avoid unnecessary clamping to support dependent drainage and prevent backflow or pressure complications.

source_original.stem: Which action is appropriate for a client with a chest tube connected to a drainage system?

options.A: Place the drainage system on the bed at chest level.
options.B: Keep the drainage system upright and below the client's chest.
options.C: Raise the system above the chest during repositioning.
options.D: Clamp the tube routinely during transport.

source_original.rationale: Keeping the chest drainage system upright and below the chest supports drainage and reduces the risk of fluid backflow. Option B is correct. Placing the system at or above chest level or routinely clamping the tube can create complications.
source_original.source_detail: Chest drainage management: keep the drainage system upright and below chest/insertion-site level to facilitate dependent drainage and prevent backflow; avoid unnecessary clamping and dependent tubing loops. Current NCBI Bookshelf chest-tube care entry live-rechecked 2026-08-15. correction_summary: Retained the chest-drainage positioning construct and key B. Tightened all options around drainage-system height and clamping, and strengthened the rationale with current NCBI nursing guidance that routine clamping is not recommended. No manufacturer-specific suction setting or tubing manipulation rule was added.

audit_findings.source_authority: Current NCBI/StatPearls plus NCBI/Open RN nursing-device guidance; NCSBN 2026 blueprint

audit_findings.claim_audit: Final item uses only directly supported system-position and clamping safety principles and does not introduce a manufacturer-specific device setting.

distractor_audit.A: Incorrect because chest-level placement does not maintain the drainage unit below the patient for dependent flow/backflow prevention.
distractor_audit.C: Incorrect because lifting above chest level can permit backflow.
distractor_audit.D: Incorrect because routine clamping is not recommended and can increase tension-pneumothorax risk.

audit_findings.ambiguity_second_answer: Only B satisfies both the upright and below-chest/insertion-site positioning principles without introducing unnecessary clamping.
audit_findings.cueing: All options are chest-tube drainage-system management actions and are parallel in scope.
audit_findings.blueprint: Reduction of Risk Potential — therapeutic device management and complication prevention.
audit_findings.independent_second_pass: Rechecked current StatPearls and Open RN/NCBI content, all four options, rationale, objective, NCSBN mapping, ambiguity and cueing. B remained uniquely correct.
